criteria.role: Is this opening explicitly an internship or co-op in software engineering, machine learning/AI research, data science, or PRODUCT management? Senior full-time, student developer without internship evidence, PROJECT management and finance roles violate this search requirement.
criteria.authorization: Does the candidate satisfy all mandatory citizenship, work authorization and visa sponsorship restrictions? If the posting omits these restrictions, choose not_stated; do not infer sponsorship from silence.
criteria.education: Does the candidate satisfy mandatory degree level, subject and enrollment requirements? Treat preferred graduate degrees as optional. Equivalent experience is an alternative; review when its adequacy is unclear.
criteria.location: Does the posting explicitly permit this candidate to work in the United States? Remote alone does not imply any country; explicit conflicting jurisdictions violate.
criteria.required_skills: Does confirmed candidate evidence satisfy all explicitly REQUIRED skills/experience? Missing preferred skills do not violate. Years thresholds are handled separately in code; missing proof of mandatory skill means ambiguous, not confirmed absence.

outcomes.satisfied: Explicit evidence confirms compatibility, or explicitly no restriction for this criterion.
outcomes.violated: Explicit mandatory restriction conflicts with an explicitly confirmed candidate fact.
outcomes.not_stated: The posting does not state the relevant requirement; compatibility cannot be confirmed.
outcomes.ambiguous: Conflicting requirements or insufficient candidate evidence to decide.

dimensions.skills: Rate coverage of stated required and preferred skills by confirmed candidate facts.
dimensions.projects: Rate demonstrated project relevance to the actual advertised responsibilities.
dimensions.responsibilities: Rate alignment of actual duties with candidate software/data work experience.
dimensions.preferences: Rate alignment with candidate stated Python/backend/data career preferences.

levels: No demonstrated alignment or missing relevant information
Substantial alignment: several direct overlaps but meaningful gaps
Strong alignment: direct evidence supports almost all important aspects
